Shinylive – licence notice
==========================
This site runs Shiny apps in the same way as Shinylive (Posit; https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive),
which runs Shiny apps in a web page using R in webR. The site's files listed below were written for
the workbench, based on Shinylive's code. They are not copies of it, but they follow its design
closely, and some parts are close to Shinylive's own code. In particular, they use the same
messages between the page, the service worker and the app's frame, with the same names
(configureProxyPath, makeRequest, openChannel and serviceworkerStart), the same kind of stand-in
for the app's WebSocket, and the same calls into Shiny that R uses to answer the app's requests:

  isolation-sw.js (the Shiny part)   based on src/shinylive-sw.ts
  assets/js/shiny-socket.js          based on src/shinylive-inject-socket.ts and src/messageportwebsocket.ts
  assets/js/shiny.js                 based on src/messageporthttp.ts, src/messageportwebsocket.ts,
                                     src/messageportwebsocket-channel.ts and src/hooks/useWebR.tsx
  assets/js/rsession.js              its R functions wb$shiny_run, wb$shiny_reader, wb$shiny_http,
                                     wb$shiny_ws_open, wb$shiny_ws_msg, wb$shiny_ws_close and
                                     wb$shiny_tick, based on the R code in src/hooks/useWebR.tsx,
                                     src/messageporthttp.ts and src/messageportwebsocket-channel.ts

(These files were compared with commit 80eb17c461d6bfd60f61d16bef92ad9c83d87434 of Shinylive's
main branch on 15 October 2026.)

Shinylive's licence applies to the parts of these files that are derived from Shinylive. Its
notice, taken from the LICENSE file in its repository, is reproduced below. (RStudio, PBC is now
called Posit Software, PBC.)
